ask_parts_not_covered.part: production data never ends up in staging
ask_parts_not_covered.why: runtime_data: policies read stored definitions only, never records or data copied between branches/environments/tenants (catalogue 'What no check can see')

ask_parts_not_covered.part: devs can only get into prod through the on-call process, not on a whim
ask_parts_not_covered.why: access reviews and change approvals happen outside definitions (catalogue 'What no check can see'); no check reads who can reach the workspace or who approved a change

assumptions: 'prod' and 'staging' are branches or environments in Xano; the workspace shows no environment tag or marker
request_human_approval is an agent-action approval step, not a dev-access gate
patients, clinical_notes and customers are the tables a team would consider production-grade data (guessed from names and schema)
confusions: The skill says to write no policy only when no part is checkable, but the partial-approximation options (table.write_location_restricted, CONF-010) are not clearly 'checkable part' versus 'approximation'. I treated them as approximations and didn't write them without asking.
The skill covers policies for a workspace with existing policy files; this workspace has no policies/ directory and no policy list, so the 'read the policies that apply' step had nothing to read.
The 'what no check can see' section is only in the CLI catalogue output, not in kit/catalogue.json. I found it by running the read-only xano policy catalogue command.
wished_for: A clear 'no policy fits' recipe for requests about access control and environments, with a sentence the assistant can give the customer
A way to express that a table is production data (an environment tag or branch marker) that a policy could read, if the platform adds one
Guidance on whether a partial approximation is allowed to be written when the user has not asked for it
why_confidence: No policy is written, so no policy achieves the goal. I am highly confident that no check can enforce either part: the catalogue explicitly lists data copies between environments and access/approval processes as unseen by any check. I did not run xano policy parse because no policy file was written.
